question: Is the site visit free?
short_answer: Free for projects of 100 kWp and above in the three sales regions; outside them a travel fee may apply.

question: How thick is the coating?
short_answer: Depends on the system: 85 µm hot-dip galvanising (GF-1, CP-1), 25 µm per side zinc-magnesium (GF-2), 15 µm anodic layer (RF-1, RP-1), 20 µm (RF-2).

question: How long does your crew take to install a 500 kWp system on a flat roof?
short_answer: The knowledge base gives an installation rate only for ground-mount structures, not for roofs.

question: Яке максимальне снігове навантаження для GF-2?
short_answer: Only English is supported.

question: Our 'flat' roof actually falls at about 7 degrees. Which of your ballasted systems would fit it?
short_answer: Neither: RF-1 and RF-2 allow at most 5° roof slope, and RP-1 starts at 10°.

question: We'd like panels on the warehouse but we've lost all the building plans. Can it still happen?
short_answer: Yes: the company can order a roof assessment from a partner engineer at the customer's cost; installation needs a positive assessment.

question: Quels documents faut-il fournir pour obtenir un devis ?
short_answer: Only English is supported.

question: How strong a wind can the south-facing flat-roof system take?
short_answer: RF-1 is rated for up to 28 m/s.

question: The carport is aluminium like your roof kits, so rust won't ever be an issue, will it?
short_answer: CP-1 is hot-dip galvanised steel, not aluminium, rated for corrosivity category C4.

question: Is there one person at your end for our region, or do we deal with a different contact each time?
short_answer: Each sales region has its own project manager, assigned after the first request based on the project location.

question: What feed-in tariff or subsidy could a 2 MWp plant get?
short_answer: The knowledge base says nothing about tariffs or subsidies.

question: The land climbs about 12% from south to north. Can the twin-post system go straight in without earthworks?
short_answer: No: GF-2 follows slopes up to 10%, so grading is recommended (not a company service); GF-1 can follow up to 15%.

question: How long until you get back to me?
short_answer: Usually within 2 working days; warranty claims within 5 working days.

question: A storm just hit our GF-1 plant with gusts of around 30 m/s. What should we do, and is any damage covered?
short_answer: Book an extra inspection (recommended after gusts above 25 m/s); damage from wind above the structural-calculation values is not covered.

question: Why does RF-1 put less weight on the roof than RF-2?
short_answer: It doesn't: RF-2 puts less load on the roof, 12 to 20 kg/m² against 18 to 30 kg/m² for RF-1.

question: The field is quite hilly. Will your team flatten it out before building?
short_answer: No: grading is recommended on steep sites but is not part of the company's services.

question: Do we have to send a truck to your warehouse to collect the steel, or does it come to us?
short_answer: Delivery to the site is included in every supply order.

question: Your posts always go 2.5 m into the ground anyway, so we can skip the soil investigation, can't we?
short_answer: No: posts usually go 1.5 to 2.5 m deep, the exact depth comes from the geotechnical survey, and every ground-mount project needs one.

question: What plant sizes is the twin-post system normally used for?
short_answer: GF-2 is typically used for plants of 1 MWp to 100 MWp.

question: How many years is the twin-post structure designed to last?
short_answer: The knowledge base gives a 15-year product warranty but no design life.
